builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Surfacing Disagreement Beats Resolving It: A Gated Ablation Study of Provenance-Weighted Memory for Multi-Agent Debate
summary: This technique replaces standard shared-memory retrieval that silently resolves contradictions by returning a single winning fact. It instead preserves contradictions and passes the ranked conflict set to the debate, at equal operational cost. The main failure risk is implementation-sensitive: conflict sets are built only over retrieved edges, so a retrieval cap can make most planted contradictions unretrievable and drastically reduce the measured benefit; additionally, once contradictions reach the prompt, some mechanisms such as a write trust-gate or provenance routing can reduce accuracy.
rationale: The paper provides a significant quality improvement on a constrained setup, but the effect depends on careful harness implementation and validation on the reader's specific workload.
technique: Provenance-weighted memory preserving contradictions for multi-agent debate

claims.statement: This technique replaces standard shared-memory retrieval that silently resolves contradictions by returning a single winning fact. It instead preserves contradictions and passes the ranked conflict set to the debate, at equal operational cost. The main failure risk is implementation-sensitive: conflict sets are built only over retrieved edges, so a retrieval cap can make most planted contradictions unretrievable and drastically reduce the measured benefit; additionally, once contradictions reach the prompt, some mechanisms such as a write trust-gate or provenance routing can reduce accuracy.
Improves F1 by +0.340 (95% CI [+0.267, +0.414]) and reduces attack success from 22/122 to 7/122 poisoned items (McNemar exact p=0.0003) at equal cost compared to winner-collapse retrieval.
